> Is there any specific place I could go to learn the language if I would move to a certain European country?

As in a region? Perhaps it would be easiest to study it in the capital, as the accent and vocabulary used there is perhaps the most characteristic for the local language. If you go east you'll start getting a lot of turkish words, north you'll get a lot of german and hungarian words, while west and south you'll start hearing the local language mixed with neighboring languages, as well as italian words and phrases. While in the capital you will have the chance to hear all variations but perhaps the cleanest version is prevalent exactly there. No matter where in the country you are, people aren't going to be speaking the standard language, but a variant influenced by other cultures, some more, some less. For an example, I live near the capital and the language we speak here has a fair amount of germanisms and turkisms. Not enough to override a language, but enough to make us speak foreign words instead of the standard ones.

Driving without a ticket is not a criminal offense but a violation of public transportation rules in a major European city. However, if you receive a fine and ignore it, a criminal complaint is filed against you, leading to court proceedings, payment of the fine, and payment of costs. If you ignore that as well, enforcement proceedings follow.

Everyone has the right to call the police, and reports of riding without a ticket are likely processed more for record-keeping than for immediate police pursuit of the individual.
